the new method allows the estimation of the spatial and temporal variation of DSSF over land, and the estimation of ARF at ground-level over land, from METEOSA-7 observation; the method is validated by comparison to ground-based measurements; the method is sensitive to AOT; the method can be applied to other satellite instruments, such as SEVIRI, MODIS and VIIRS, with the same accuracy.

we propose a new method to estimate the spatial distribution of aerosol forcing at ground level from the visible broadband of a geostationary satellite instrument, and we demonstrate the feasibility of the method with a case study.

1. the proposed method is a promising approach to retrieve the aerosol radiatiive forcing (ARF) at ground level over land from the METEOSAT-2nd Generation satellite, 2. the accuracy of the method is sufficient for the purpose of aerosol monitoring, and 3. the method is robust and applicable to a large number of aerosol types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the retrieval of DSSF and ARF from the visible METEOSAT-1 broadband channel, which is the most appropriate for regional applications.
a method to retrieve the spatial and temporal distribution of DSSF, and ARF at ground and over land, from the visible broadband of a geostationary satellite.

the development of a new methodology to retrieve the aerosol radiating impact on solar radiation at the ground, and to provide a first estimate of the aerosol forcing at ground level and on land, from METEOSA-7 observations, for a large area of Europe and Africa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this method is able to retrieve the spatial and temporal evolution of DSSF and ARF at ground and over land, in cloud-free atmosphere, with an accuracy assessment of ±20 W m − 2 (5%) in 70% and ±40 W m − 1 in 90% (relative) of the cases.
the method is able to reproduce the ground-based measurements in 70% to 90% of all situations.

the proposed method allows retrieving the DSSF with a good accuracy (20 W m − 2) for a variety of situations and that the ARF at the surface can be estimated with an accuracy of the order of 100 W m − 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose to use a simple method based on a radiative transfer model to estimate the solar radiative forcing at the surface and in the cloudless atmosphere from satellite measurements, with an accuracy better than 20% for the surface forcing and 10% for the forcing in the cloudless column.
the method provides a good estimation of the aerosol forcing at ground level in the case of cloudless atmosphere.

we have developed a method to retrieve the solar radiation reaching the surface in clear sky, over land, at the spatial and temporal resolution of a satellite image, and to estimate the aerosol forcing at ground level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple and robust method is available to estimate DSSF and ARF at ground-level, over land and in cloudless conditions.
